item.text:
**Verdict:** mixed, leaning negative. Erdoğan’s 2024 record contains some real welfare-relevant actions, especially post-earthquake housing, refugee safety management, and a targeted pension increase, but I did not find strong 2024 evidence of broad improvements in health, education, water, sanitation, or food security at scale. The strongest counterevidence is that relief often looked narrow, delayed, or politically managed rather than a systematic expansion of basic services.

|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | Turkey completes new homes in area hit by devastating earthquake | Reuters | 2024-02-03 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/turkey-completes-new-homes-in-area-hit-by-devastating-earthquake-3291916) | Erdoğan’s government handed over 7,275 homes in Hatay and said more reconstruction was coming. This is concrete housing access for earthquake survivors and the clearest direct welfare improvement I found. | 6B.2; also 5B.6, 5B.9, 5B.10 |
| Positive | Turkey to work for Syrian migrants to return home safely, minister says | Reuters | 2024-12-09 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/turkey-to-work-for-syrian-migrants-to-return-home-safely-minister-says-3760765) | Turkey said it would open the Yayladagi border gate to manage safe, voluntary return and prevent congestion after Assad’s fall. This is a limited but real welfare-oriented response for displaced Syrians. | 6B.2; also 5B.8, 5B.9 |
| Positive | Turkey - Socially Inclusive Green Transition Project | World Bank | 2024-03-06 | [link](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099031124170520652) | The project aims to improve women and youth economic opportunities, including finance for women- and youth-led MSMEs, local infrastructure, and support in less developed areas. This is an inclusion-oriented social-policy signal, though it is indirect evidence about Erdoğan’s own priorities. | 6B.2; also 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.10 |
| Positive | World Bank to Support Women, Youth Owned Small Businesses and Industry Adapt to Green Transition in Türkiye | World Bank | 2024-04-01 | [link](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/03/29/world-bank-to-support-women-youth-owned-small-businesses-and-industry-adapt-to-green-transition-in-turkiye) | The World Bank said the financing was intended to make the transition more equitable and inclusive, especially for women, youth, and vulnerable groups in less developed areas. This supports a fairness-oriented welfare reading, but remains programmatic rather than a broad state-service expansion. | 6B.2; also 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.10 |
| Weak positive | Türkiye co-sponsored a joint letter calling for an immediate and permanent ceasefire | UN / UNISPAL | 2024-11-01 | [link](https://www.un.org/unispal/document/joint-call-to-halt-arms-transfers-to-israel-signed-by-52-member-states-and-two-international-organizations-letter-from-turkiye-a-79-572-s-2024-802/) | Türkiye co-sponsored a call for a ceasefire, civilian protection, and an arms-transfer halt. This reflects humanitarian concern, but it is only indirect welfare evidence and mostly about external policy. | 6B.2; also 6B.1, 5B.9 |
| Negative | Turkey: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/turkey/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House says AKP politics favored Sunni Muslims, Kurdish parties faced harassment, women and LGBT people remained politically marginalized, and refugees faced severe restrictions and anti-foreigner rhetoric. That points away from equal access to state protection and social support. | 6B.2; also 5B.8, 6B.1 |
| Negative | World Report 2024: Türkiye | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | [link](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/turkey) | HRW says women and girls still lacked effective protection from domestic violence, anti-LGBT hate speech was central to the campaign, and Pride events were repeatedly banned with arrests. This is strong evidence that basic social protection was not being expanded in a broadly rights-respecting way. | 6B.2; also 6B.1, 5B.8 |
| Negative | Turkey ousts 3 elected pro-Kurdish mayors from office and replaces them with state officials | AP | 2024-11-04 | [link](https://apnews.com/article/5aba9ba471ecc222c6fbba535a9e6546) | The government removed elected pro-Kurdish mayors and replaced them with state officials over terrorism-related charges. That suggests politically selective control over local authority, not neutral access to public services. | 6B.2; also 5B.8, 4B.10 |
| Negative | Shock, confusion as Turkey seizes earthquake survivors' homes | Reuters | 2024-03-18 | [link](https://www.reuters.com/commodities/shock-confusion-as-turkey-seizes-earthquake-survivors-homes-2024-03-18/) | Reuters reported deed transfers in Hatay to the Treasury under an urban-planning amendment, alarming survivors. This is a serious trust and housing-security failure in a disaster zone, cutting against a welfare-first reading. | 6B.2; also 5B.8, 5B.9, 6B.1 |
| Negative | Turkey to lift minimum retirement pay, impose minimum corporate tax | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-07-16 | [link](https://theprint.in/world/turkey-to-lift-minimum-retirement-pay-impose-minimum-corporate-tax/2176793/) | Reuters portrayed the minimum-pension increase as targeted relief in an inflationary environment, closer to discontent management than a broad social-protection reform. It helps some retirees, but it looks narrow and politically selective. | 6B.2; also 5B.7, 5B.8, 5B.9 |

Search gap: I did not find strong 2024 primary evidence of broad improvements in health care access, schooling, clean water, sanitation, or food security. The evidence base is strongest for housing, refugee safety, and limited social protection, and weaker for sustained system-wide access to basic services.
